info.bio:
Ravi Shankar (nacido el 7 de abril, 1920 en Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, India) es un músico bengalí conocido mundialmente por ser un virtuoso del sitar.

Discípulo de Allauddin Khan (fundador del Maihar gharana de música hindú clásica), Pandit Ravi Shankar es posiblemente el instrumentista hindú más reconocido, es conocido por ser pionero en la traída del poder de la tradición de música hindú clásica, así como por músico hindú y sus ejecutantes en general.

scenes.name: La India en el pop: sitar y raga rock
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: La música india se convirtió en la metáfora sonora central del LSD: el dron del sitar y la longitud de las piezas reproducían la dislocación del tiempo, el timbre vibraba en el cuerpo, había un impulso religioso y, a oídos occidentales, ni ego ni formato de tres minutos. Entró en el pop con «See My Friends» de los Kinks, «Heart Full of Soul» de los Yardbirds y la banda sonora de Help!, donde los Beatles descubrieron el sitar poco después de su primer ácido. Jim Dickson, mánager de los Byrds, tenía relación con World Pacific, que grababa a Ravi Shankar (Portrait of a Genius, Sound of the Sitar); Tony Hall recomendaba vivir con sus discos y Harrison quedó deslumbrado al verlo en el Festival Hall. En 1966 llegaron «Eight Miles High», «Shapes of Things», «Paint It, Black» y «Tomorrow Never Knows».

scenes.name: Alicia, la locura y el regreso a la infancia
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Al final de 1966 el LSD llevó al pop de vuelta a la infancia y a la locura. Los Beatles empezaron el 24 de noviembre «Strawberry Fields Forever», un viaje de Lennon hacia abajo, no hacia atrás, al orfanato junto a su casa, «psicoanálisis con música», unida por Geoff Emerick a partir de dos tomas; luego «When I’m Sixty-Four» y «Penny Lane». En Navidad la BBC aplazó el Alice in Wonderland de Jonathan Miller, sin cabezas de animal, con el sitar de Ravi Shankar y rodado en un hospital militar de víctimas de neurosis de guerra: un catálogo de psicosis. Grace Slick llevó «White Rabbit» a Jefferson Airplane; Syd Barrett escribía sobre el mundo de Lewis Carroll. Proliferaban los discos sobre la locura («They’re Coming to Take Me Away, Ha-Haaa!», «Pandora’s Golden Heebie Jeebies» de los Association), y en el corazón secreto del año, la tristeza frágil de «How Can We Hang On to a Dream» de Tim Hardin.

The song’s Elvin Jones-style drums, Coltrane convulsions and timestretching Shankar drones fused two staples of sixties minority taste: free jazz and Indian classical music. Both had been the period’s secret soundtrack – the…

The Byrds had been immersed in Ravi Shankar through their co-manager, Jim Dickson. He had strong affiliations with World Pacific Records, who recorded several Shankar albums during the mid-sixties – most notably Portrait of a Genius (1965) and Sound of the Sitar (1966). mentions.text: …in the subcontinent’s music. ‘You can even dig Indian music,’ wrote Tony Hall in his Record Mirror column during January 1966, after seeing a Shankar concert. ‘Try buying one of his albums sometime. And live with it. He’s something else.’ Indian music was shaping up as the central aural metaphor…

Asked about psychedelic music, Crosby observed that Archie…

He expounded on his passion for the sitar, recently awakened by seeing Ravi Shankar play at the Festival Hall. ‘I couldn’t believe it,’ he said. ‘It was just like everything you have ever thought of as great all coming out at once.’…

The White Rabbit was performed by Wilfrid Brambell, who had played Paul McCartney’s grandfather in A Hard Day’s Night, while Ravi Shankar had been George Harrison’s friend and mentor during 1966. podcast.title: Reunion with Norah Jones
podcast.body: Norah Jones was reunited with her father, Ravi Shankar, when she was 18, and they began to build a relationship. However, media coverage surrounding her fame often misrepresented their connection, causing distress within her family. "And I had my band. We were having fun. There was also a weird thing that was happening because my dad and I had been reunited when I was 18 and we started to really find our relationship and it was great and it was really nice to have that."
